diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/vplan-simplify-recipes.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/vplan-simplify-recipes.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d78c6512d9ae
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/vplan-simplify-recipes.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+; Test the simplify-recipes VPlan transform that simplifies recipe patterns.
+
+; RUN: opt -passes='vplan-test<create-loop-regions;widen-from-metadata;simplify-recipes>' -disable-output %s | FileCheck %s
+
+; Check that 'or %val, 0' is simplified, so store uses %val directly.
+; CHECK-LABEL: VPlan ' for UF>=1' {
+; CHECK: <x1> vector loop: {
+; CHECK:   vector.body:
+; CHECK:     EMIT ir<%val> = load ir<%gep>
+; CHECK:     EMIT store ir<%val>, ir<%gep>
+; CHECK:   No successors
+; CHECK: }
+
+define void @test_simplify(ptr %A, i64 %N) {
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
+  %gep = getelementptr i32, ptr %A, i64 %iv
+  %val = load i32, ptr %gep
+  ; Identity: or X, 0 -> X (should be simplified away)
+  %result = or i32 %val, 0, !vplan.widen !{}
+  store i32 %result, ptr %gep
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %iv.next, %N
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix masked_cond expansion.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit fixes masked_cond expansion during VPlan conversion to concrete recipes by reversing the operands of a generated VPInstruction::LogicalAnd from {condition, mask} to {mask, condition}. Corresponding LoopVectorize predicated early-exit tests update generated vector select expectations so the prior active mask is the select condition and the new condition is the selected value.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; VPInstruction::LogicalAnd; three_early_exits; single_exit_in_conditional_block; diamond_with_2_early_exits
Behavioral change: Changes the operand order used to construct a LogicalAnd VPInstruction for masked_cond expansion.; Changes generated predicated early-exit mask composition, as reflected by updated vector select operands in single-exit, multiple-exit, and interleaved-exit tests.; Corrects mask/condition semantics during conversion from abstract VPlan instructions to concrete recipes.
Assertion or trace link: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; VPInstruction::LogicalAnd; masked_cond; predicated early exits
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests exercise predicated early exits rather than the reported crash-62b480.cpp attachment.; No retrieved test asserts or reproduces 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe'.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan transforms; predicated early-exit vectorization
Causal explanation: This is a real VPlan implementation change in LoopVectorize and changes the operands used while concretizing a VPlan, making it more relevant than test-only changes. Nevertheless, the patch only changes LogicalAnd operand ordering for masked-condition expansion; it neither inserts phi-like recipes nor changes their placement in VPBasicBlock recipe storage. The available evidence supports a possible indirect VPlan interaction, but not a direct causal path to the phi-like-after-non-phi assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.15
Build risk: Production VPlan transformation code changes together with multiple generated-IR expectations.; Affected tests cover predicated single-exit, multiple-exit, and interleaved early-exit loops.; The change can alter vector mask semantics and generated select operand order.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/predicated-multiple-exits.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/predicated-multiple-exits.ll
index e15d4fde3d70..f54f6ec768bc 100644
--- a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/predicated-multiple-exits.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/predicated-multiple-exits.ll
@@ -715,0 +716,135 @@ loop.end:
+
+; When the else branch is speculatively executed for iv < 2, `sub nuw` wraps
+; producing poison. This poison condition is processed first in RPO.
+; Test for https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/187061.
+define i32 @diamond_exit_poison_from_speculated_branch() {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @diamond_exit_poison_from_speculated_branch() {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[VECTOR_PH:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[VECTOR_PH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[VECTOR_BODY:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[VECTOR_BODY]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = freeze <4 x i1> <i1 poison, i1 poison, i1 true, i1 true>
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = call i1 @llvm.vector.reduce.or.v4i1(<4 x i1> [[TMP0]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[TMP1]], label %[[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_CHECK:.*]], label %[[MIDDLE_BLOCK:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[MIDDLE_BLOCK]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP_END:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_CHECK]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[FIRST_ACTIVE_LANE:%.*]] = call i64 @llvm.experimental.cttz.elts.i64.v4i1(<4 x i1> <i1 poison, i1 poison, i1 true, i1 true>, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP2:%.*]] = extractelement <4 x i1> <i1 poison, i1 poison, i1 false, i1 false>, i64 [[FIRST_ACTIVE_LANE]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[TMP2]], label %[[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_0:.*]], label %[[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_1:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP3:%.*]] = extractelement <4 x i32> <i32 10, i32 11, i32 1, i32 2>, i64 [[FIRST_ACTIVE_LANE]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP_END]]
+; CHECK:       [[VECTOR_EARLY_EXIT_0]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[UNREACHABLE_EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE_EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @llvm.trap()

Summary: Relands vectorization support for overflow intrinsics. It restores field-sensitive intrinsic declaration type selection for struct-return vector intrinsics and adds extensive tests showing widened overflow calls, vector struct extraction, and vector-loop/middle-block generation for overflow operations.
Changed symbols: VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe::execute; test_overflow_intrinsic; uadd_with_overflow_i32; sadd_with_overflow_i32
Behavioral change: Restores filtering of struct-return contained types so only fields supported as vector intrinsic overloads contribute to the vector intrinsic declaration.; Enables LoopVectorize to widen signed and unsigned overflow intrinsics returning `{value, overflow-flag}` structs.; Generates vector overflow calls, extracts vector result and overflow fields, converts vector overflow flags, and emits vector-loop plus middle-block control flow for covered tests.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: The commit materially expands the set of loops for which LoopVectorize builds VPlans, including loops with multi-result overflow intrinsic recipes.; No retrieved hunk identifies crash-62b480.cpp or adds a regression test for the reported phi-like-recipe ordering assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlan recipe execution for widened intrinsics
Causal explanation: By enabling new multi-result intrinsic vectorization cases, this change can cause VPlan construction and recipe storage to be exercised for loops previously left scalar, making it a plausible indirect trigger for a vectorizer assertion. However, the visible implementation change is confined to intrinsic declaration type selection, while the reported failure is specifically a phi-like versus non-phi recipe ordering invariant. No visible candidate hunk changes VPRecipeBuilder, phi insertion order, or recipe-container ordering.
Causal confidence: 0.20

steps.subject: [VPlan] Use target's index type for {First,Last}ActiveLane instead of i64 (#186361)

evidence: Changes target-dependent scalar types and casts for FirstActiveLane and LastActiveLane recipes.
Does not alter VPlan block recipe ordering, phi insertion, or the verifier's phi-like ordering condition.
features: active-lane, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize, riscv, target-index-type
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan change replaces hard-coded i64 handling for FirstActiveLane/LastActiveLane-related values with types inferred from the VPlan and target DataLayout. It initializes VPTypeAnalysis with the plan DataLayout, derives constants and casts from inferred scalar types, and changes mask-to-EVL conversion from an unconditional zext to zext-or-trunc behavior. The accompanying RISC-V tests verify that active-lane indices use i64 on RV64 and i32 on RV32.
Changed symbols: VPTypeAnalysis::VPTypeAnalysis; VPInstruction::generate; VPlanTransforms::adjustFixedOrderRecurrences; VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; optimizeMaskToEVL
Behavioral change: VPlan type analysis now retains Plan.getDataLayout(), enabling target-dependent scalar/index-type decisions.; FirstActiveLane/LastActiveLane-adjacent constants are created using inferred scalar types rather than hard-coded i64.; Mask-to-EVL lowering uses createScalarZExtOrTrunc instead of always creating a zext.; Generated vector IR for RISC-V active-lane operations can use i32 indices on 32-bit targets rather than i64.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPRecipe; FirstActiveLane; LastActiveLane
Reproducer link: No retrieved hunk mentions crash-62b480.cpp, -O3 compilation, or the 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' assertion.; The added reproducer coverage is target-specific RISC-V live-out and early-exit lowering, not VPlan recipe ordering.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPTypeAnalysis; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: The commit is in the implicated VPlan subsystem and changes recipe construction/lowering inputs through type inference, so it is not unrelated. However, the retrieved changes concern scalar index types, casts, and active-lane constants; they do not add, move, or reorder phi-like recipes in VPlan blocks or SmallVector-backed recipe storage. The available evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect link to the reported ordering assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.13
Build risk: Adds RISC-V LoopVectorize regression coverage for both RV64 and RV32 active-lane index typing.; Changes target-dependent VPlan type inference and IR cast generation, creating cross-target code-generation regression risk.; No retrieved test exercises the reported phi-like-recipe ordering assertion or the supplied C++ attachment.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Sink single-scalar replicates in licm (#187047)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan LICM change permits sinking unpredicated VPReplicateRecipe instances when they have already been narrowed to single-scalar form. Previously LICM rejected every replicate recipe; now it rejects only non-single-scalar replicates and asserts that predicated replicates were transformed into replicate regions earlier. The test updates primarily reflect computations moving from vector-body locations into later blocks such as middle blocks.
Changed symbols: licm(VPlan &Plan); VPReplicateRecipe; VPReplicateRecipe::isPredicated; VPReplicateRecipe::isSingleScalar
Behavioral change: VPlan LICM no longer unconditionally excludes VPReplicateRecipe objects from sinking.; Only unpredicated single-scalar replicate recipes may be sunk; predicated replicates remain required to have been transformed into replicate regions, and non-single-scalar replicates remain excluded.; Eligible replicate computations can be moved to a sink block using the existing placement before that block's first non-phi recipe.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPReplicateRecipe; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe; recipe ordering
Reproducer link: The retrieved tests cover recurrence, LCSSA, induction-variable, and uniform-operation vectorization output changes rather than crash-62b480.cpp.; No retrieved hunk contains the reported 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; VPlan LICM
Causal explanation: This is the strongest structural match among the candidates because it expands VPlan recipe motion and thus can alter recipe placement within VPlan blocks. The visible LICM context places moved candidates before the destination's first non-phi recipe, which appears intended to preserve phi-before-non-phi ordering; moreover, the newly eligible recipes are VPReplicateRecipe objects rather than explicitly phi-like recipes. Thus the change plausibly perturbs plan ordering indirectly, but the retrieved evidence does not show a path that inserts a phi-like recipe after a non-phi recipe.
Causal confidence: 0.23
Build risk: Changes VPlan LICM eligibility and recipe movement, which can affect generated control flow and placement-sensitive vectorization lowering.; Includes several LoopVectorize output-check updates spanning recurrences, LCSSA, induction users, and uniform operations.; The new assertion on predicated replicates may expose pipeline-order assumptions in debug/assertion-enabled builds.; No retrieved regression test directly checks VPlan phi-like recipe ordering.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix wrap-flags on WidenInduction unroll (#187710)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan change preserves induction-operation flags during unrolling. It adds no-wrap flag accessors to the relevant VPlan instruction abstraction, changes UnrollState::unrollWidenInductionByUF to obtain fast-math and no-wrap flags from the VP widening-induction recipe rather than solely from the scalar induction descriptor, and uses the new no-wrap accessor when constructing an explicit-vector-length iteration increment. The accompanying LoopVectorize tests now expect nsw flags on unrolled vector induction-step additions.
Changed symbols: hasNoWrapFlags; getNoWrapFlags; UnrollState::unrollWidenInductionByUF; VPlanTransforms::addExplicitVectorLength
Behavioral change: Unrolled VPWidenIntOrFpInductionRecipe instances retain fast-math flags and no-wrap flags when their per-unroll-part recipes are constructed.; Explicit-vector-length current-iteration increments obtain both no-wrap properties through CanonicalIVIncrement::getNoWrapFlags rather than reconstructing the pair at the call site.; Generated vector induction-step additions may now carry nsw, as covered by updated LoopVectorize IR checks.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPRecipe; phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: No retrieved test or hunk references crash-62b480.cpp or an assertion failure.; The changed tests exercise decreasing and non-constant-start induction variables with unrolling.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan unrolling; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: The commit is in the affected VPlan/LoopVectorize subsystem and changes construction metadata for widened induction recipes during unrolling, so it can influence the form of plans built for induction-heavy loops. However, the retrieved changes only propagate arithmetic flags; they do not add, move, erase, or reorder phi-like and non-phi recipes, and contain no direct evidence involving SmallVector-backed recipe storage or the reported ordering assertion. The older first-parent-distance-4 LoopVectorize flag context is not attributed as a change by this candidate.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Implementation changes are accompanied by updated LoopVectorize IR-output tests for multiple induction forms.; The new VPlan.h accessors are consumed by both VPlan unrolling and explicit-vector-length construction, giving the change cross-component compile coverage.; No assertion-reproducer test was added in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Extends VPlan LICM sinking to permit unpredicated VPReplicateRecipe instances when they have already been narrowed to single-scalar replicates. Previously all replicate recipes were excluded from sinking; now only non-single-scalar replicates remain excluded, with an assertion that predicated replicates were transformed into replicate regions earlier.
Changed symbols: licm; VPReplicateRecipe; VPReplicateRecipe::isPredicated; VPReplicateRecipe::isSingleScalar; exit_phi_sunk_def; for_phi_removed; unused_recurrence
Behavioral change: Allows LICM to sink single-scalar, unpredicated VPReplicateRecipe objects instead of unconditionally skipping all replicates.; Retains exclusion of non-single-scalar replicates because replicateByVF does not correctly handle sunk non-single-scalar recipes under unrolling.; Introduces an invariant check that predicated replicates must already have been converted to replicate regions before this sinking path.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPReplicateRecipe; phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; The surrounding retrieved VPlan LICM context moves sink candidates before getFirstNonPhi().
Reproducer link: Updated tests include LCSSA exit-phi and first-order-recurrence cases, showing that sinking changes generated vector-loop placement.; No crash-62b480.cpp reproducer or direct phi-order assertion test is shown.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan LICM; VPlan recipe placement and sinking
Causal explanation: This candidate directly changes whether a VPlan recipe can be moved between basic blocks, making it materially closer to a phi/non-phi recipe-order invariant than the other candidates. The surrounding context shows the sinking mechanism placing candidates before the first non-phi recipe, which appears intended to preserve phi-first ordering, not violate it. Still, enabling a previously excluded VPReplicateRecipe class changes the set of recipes subject to that movement and can expose ordering interactions in plans with header/exit phis. The retrieved evidence does not establish that it produces the reported assertion or that the attachment contains such a replicate.
Causal confidence: 0.54
Build risk: The new path asserts in debug builds if a predicated VPReplicateRecipe reaches LICM without prior conversion to a replicate region.; Tests change across IV users, first-order recurrences, LCSSA exit phis, and uniform operations, indicating broad code-generation placement effects.; No build-system or configuration-file changes are shown.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix wrap-flags on WidenInduction unroll (#187710)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Fixes preservation of induction-operation flags during VPlan unrolling. It adds VPIRFlags helpers to identify and retrieve no-wrap flags, copies fast-math and no-wrap flags from VPWidenIntOrFpInductionRecipe during unroll, and uses the canonical increment's complete no-wrap flag set when creating the explicit-vector-length current-iteration increment.
Changed symbols: VPIRFlags::hasNoWrapFlags; VPIRFlags::getNoWrapFlags; UnrollState::unrollWidenInductionByUF; VPlanTransforms::addExplicitVectorLength; VPWidenIntOrFpInductionRecipe
Behavioral change: Preserves signed and unsigned no-wrap flags when unrolling widened integer or floating-point inductions.; Preserves fast-math flags when the widened induction recipe carries them.; Uses getNoWrapFlags() for the explicit-vector-length current-iteration increment instead of reconstructing the flag pair at the call site.; Changes expected vector induction increments to carry nsw in affected LoopVectorize tests.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPlanUnroll; LoopVectorize; No "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" assertion, phi-like recipe ordering logic, or SmallVector recipe-storage change is shown in the candidate hunks.
Reproducer link: The tests exercise decreasing and non-constant-start vector inductions and validate nsw propagation.; No crash-62b480.cpp reproducer or ordering-assertion regression test is present.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan unrolling; widened induction and explicit-vector-length construction
Causal explanation: The candidate is in the relevant VPlan and LoopVectorize area, and unrolling can duplicate recipes, including induction-related plan content. But the actual changes concern IR semantic flags on induction arithmetic, not recipe ordering, insertion positions, phi-like classification, or recipe container management. The distance-4 LoopVectorize VPRecipeBuilder flag hunk is older context only and is not a change made by this candidate.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: Adds VPlan flag-query APIs and updates their consumers in unroll and explicit-vector-length construction.; LoopVectorize tests now require nsw on generated vector induction additions, providing targeted coverage for the changed behavior.; No build-system or configuration-file changes are shown.

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Materialize VectorTripCount in narrowInterleaveGroups. (#182146)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change updates narrowInterleaveGroups to materialize the vector trip count using its newly narrowed step, propagate that step to the induction increment and VFxUF uses, and handle scalar-epilogue topology explicitly. It also changes vector-preheader recipe insertion: the narrowed-step definition is built at the beginning of the vector preheader, while vector-trip-count materialization is inserted immediately after that step definition to maintain def-use order.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::narrowInterleaveGroups; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount; LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan
Behavioral change: narrowInterleaveGroups computes whether the middle block requires a scalar epilogue and bails out for unsupported tail-folding/topology configurations.; The narrowed vector step is materialized into the vector trip-count calculation, installed as the induction increment operand, and substituted for uses of Plan.getVFxUF().; The narrowed-step recipe is inserted at VectorPH->begin(), and materializeVectorTripCount inserts its generated recipes after the step definition when that definition belongs to the vector preheader.; executePlan now passes BestVPlan.getVFxUF() to the updated vectorization execution path.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; preheader phi; recipe insertion order
Reproducer link: Adds a regression explicitly described as ensuring LoopVectorize does not crash when connecting an epilog vector loop with an interleave group and a preheader phi.; The added test is not the reported crash-62b480.cpp attachment and does not display the reported assertion text.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan transforms; narrow interleave groups; epilog vectorization
Causal explanation: This is the strongest visible ordering-related candidate. The change explicitly inserts a new non-phi narrowed-step recipe at the beginning of VectorPH. If that preheader already contains a phi-like recipe for the affected plan, this placement can produce exactly the invalid ordering described by the issue: a phi-like recipe after a non-phi recipe. The added no-crash test involving a preheader phi and epilog connection further demonstrates that this code path handles phi-bearing vectorization cases. The supplied hunks do not prove that VectorPH contains such a phi for crash-62b480.cpp, so the link remains probabilistic.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Updates VPlan replicate-region handling for scalar VF plans, including dissolving replicate regions even when they have live-outs, avoiding vector element extraction for scalar VF, and converting predicated PHI recipes into scalar PHIs during region conversion. The change directly creates and replaces phi-like VPlan recipes while restructuring recipes in replicated regions.
Changed symbols: convertRecipesInRegionBlocksToSingleScalar; replicateReplicateRegionsByVF; VPlanTransforms::replicateByVF; VPPredInstPHIRecipe; VPPhi; VPBuilder::createScalarPhi
Behavioral change: Skips ExtractElement recipe creation when the VF is scalar, because operands are already scalar.; Converts a VPPredInstPHIRecipe into a newly created scalar VPPhi with poison and predicate operands, replaces all uses, and erases the old predicated PHI recipe.; Allows replicate-region processing for scalar VF even when the region has live-outs; vector VF still skips live-out regions because scalar-result packing is unimplemented.; Adds an early scalar-VF-only path in replicateByVF that dissolves replicate regions rather than performing the normal VF replication flow.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; phi-like recipe; VPPredInstPHIRecipe; VPPhi; VPRecipe ordering
Reproducer link: Could affect -O3 LoopVectorize plans containing predicated regions, scalar VF handling, or live-out values.; No supplied hunk demonstrates the crash-62b480.cpp reproducer or the reported assertion firing.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanUnroll
Causal explanation: This is a strong candidate because it edits the VPlan recipe-construction and replacement path for PHI-like recipes. In particular, it creates a scalar VPPhi while traversing/converting region recipes and removes the prior VPPredInstPHIRecipe. The reported failure is specifically an invariant that phi-like recipes must precede non-phi recipes, so any insertion-point or traversal-order interaction in this conversion can directly produce that class of malformed recipe ordering. The retrieved hunks do not show the insertion-point implementation or a reproducing test, so the exact ordering violation is not proven.
Causal confidence: 0.72

Summary: This commit restructures VPlan-native LoopVectorize runtime-check handling for epilogue vectorization. It moves runtime-check attachment out of LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan and into processLoopInVPlanNativePath, derives branch-weight information from the loop latch there, replaces a boolean epilogue argument with EpilogueVectorizationKind, and changes VPlanTransforms::addMinimumIterationCheck so comparison/branch recipes can be placed in a supplied check block while ExpandSCEV recipes remain in the entry block at the designated ExpandSCEV insertion point.
Changed symbols: processLoopInVPlanNativePath; LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan; LoopVectorizePass::processLoop; VPlanTransforms::addMinimumIterationCheck; EpilogueVectorizationKind; attachRuntimeChecks
Behavioral change: Runtime checks are no longer attached to BestVPlan inside executePlan; the VPlan-native path attaches them after plan selection, using branch-weight metadata from the loop-latch terminator.; The executePlan epilogue-mode interface changes from a boolean to the EpilogueVectorizationKind enum, and its caller explicitly identifies main-loop vectorization.; Minimum-iteration compare and branch recipes may now be inserted into CheckBlock instead of unconditionally into EntryVPBB.; ExpandSCEV recipes for the minimum-iteration check are explicitly inserted in EntryVPBB using getExpandSCEVInsertPt, separating their placement from the compare/branch placement.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Reworks AnyOf/Or reduction handling so the Or predicate is first represented by a VPInstruction::ComputeReductionResult and then consumed by ComputeAnyOfResult. The change updates construction of final reduction results and FindIV-reduction results, generation of ComputeAnyOfResult, and epilogue-plan preparation so an intermediate Or ComputeReductionResult is not independently selected when it feeds ComputeAnyOfResult.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::addReductionResultComputation; preparePlanForEpilogueVectorLoop; VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions; VPInstruction::generate; UnrollState::unrollBlock
Behavioral change: AnyOf reductions now create a ComputeReductionResult for the Or reduction and pass that result to ComputeAnyOfResult instead of passing the unreduced Or value directly.; VPInstruction::generate for ComputeAnyOfResult now reads its predicate operand as lane 0 rather than combining predicate operands with generated vector Or operations and CreateOrReduce.; Epilogue-plan preparation excludes a ComputeReductionResult from independent consideration when that recipe feeds ComputeAnyOfResult.; Reduction-result user handling now skips ComputeReductionResult users generally when they are not the final result, alongside the existing FindIV-specific handling.
Assertion or trace link: The modified preparePlanForEpilogueVectorLoop returns a SmallVector<Instruction *> and changes which VPlan reduction recipes are considered.; The patch does not contain the exact assertion text "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" and does not explicitly modify phi-like recipe classification.

Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms; VPlanRecipes; VPlan epilogue vector-loop preparation

evidence: Changes VPInstruction call operand accounting and VPlan memory-access validation during construction.
Its assertions concern unexpected memory-reading recipes, not phi-like recipes following non-phi recipes.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan change makes VPInstruction call handling explicit: it determines the called-function operand for masked and unmasked call recipes, uses that logic for call operand counts, and classifies calls as memory-reading/writing unless their callee is marked doesNotAccessMemory. It also tightens VPlan dereferenceability checking around VPIR basic blocks and adds LoopVectorize early-exit tests involving unary operations and calls.
Changed symbols: getCalledFnOperandIndex; getCalledFunction; VPInstruction::getNumOperandsForOpcode; VPInstruction::opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory; areAllLoadsDereferenceable; VPInstruction::VPInstruction; early_exit_with_fneg; early_exit_with_extractvalue
Behavioral change: For VPInstruction call recipes, identifies the called Function as the final operand for unmasked calls and the penultimate operand for masked calls.; Computes a call recipe's logical operand count from the called-function operand position rather than relying on the previous last-operand test.; Makes opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory report memory access for calls whose direct callee is not marked doesNotAccessMemory.; Extends the areAllLoadsDereferenceable block condition to include VPIRBasicBlock and asserts that a non-load recipe encountered there is not memory-reading.; Adds early-exit vectorization coverage for fneg and a call to llvm.smul.with.overflow.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; VPInstruction; The newly visible assertion is "unexpected recipe reading memory", not "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe".; No retrieved hunk directly manipulates phi-like recipe classification, recipe-list ordering, or SmallVector-backed recipe storage.
Reproducer link: New tests exercise LoopVectorize early-exit plans containing call-like VPInstructions, but they do not reproduce the supplied crash attachment or check the reported ordering assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan construction; VPInstruction recipe semantics
Causal explanation: This is relevant because changing call operand accounting and memory classification can change VPlan construction and validation for loops containing calls. However, the retrieved changes are confined to call/memory semantics and dereferenceability validation; they contain no explicit recipe insertion, reordering, or phi-like-recipe handling. Summary: This VPlan change makes VPInstruction call handling explicit: it determines the called-function operand for masked and unmasked call recipes, uses that logic for call operand counts, and classifies calls as memory-reading/writing unless their callee is marked doesNotAccessMemory. It also tightens VPlan dereferenceability checking around VPIR basic blocks and adds LoopVectorize early-exit tests involving unary operations and calls.
Changed symbols: getCalledFnOperandIndex; getCalledFunction; VPInstruction::getNumOperandsForOpcode; VPInstruction::opcodeMayReadOrWriteFromMemory; areAllLoadsDereferenceable; VPInstruction::VPInstruction; early_exit_with_fneg; early_exit_with_extractvalue

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/splice-cost.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/splice-cost.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..f99e61d70404
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/splice-cost.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output -debug-only=loop-vectorize 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; REQUIRES: asserts
+target triple = "aarch64"
+
+; CHECK: Cost of 1 for VF 2: EMIT vp<{{.*}}> = first-order splice
+; CHECK: Cost of 3 for VF vscale x 2: EMIT vp<{{.*}}> = first-order splice
+
+define void @foo(ptr noalias %in, ptr noalias %out, i64 %n) "target-features"="+sve" {
+entry:
+  %load.prev = load i64, ptr %in, align 8
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %indvars.iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.iv.next, %for.body ]
+  %prev = phi i64 [ %load.prev, %entry ], [ %load.cur, %for.body ]
+  %indvars.iv.next = add nuw nsw i64 %indvars.iv, 1
+  %arrayidx.load = getelementptr inbounds nuw i64, ptr %in, i64 %indvars.iv.next
+  %load.cur = load i64, ptr %arrayidx.load
+  %add = add i64 %load.cur, %prev
+  %arrayidx.store = getelementptr inbounds nuw i64, ptr %out, i64 %indvars.iv
+  store i64 %add, ptr %arrayidx.store
+  %exitcond.not = icmp eq i64 %indvars.iv.next, %n
+  br i1 %exitcond.not, label %for.cond.cleanup, label %for.body, !llvm.loop !0
+
+for.cond.cleanup:
+  ret void
+}
+
+!0 = distinct !{!0, !1, !2}
+!1 = !{!"llvm.loop.mustprogress"}
+!2 = !{!"llvm.loop.unroll.disable"}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit corrects first-order-recurrence splice cost modeling by removing construction of an explicit splice mask and instead requesting TargetTransformInfo splice cost with an empty mask and index -1. The same cost-model correction is applied in VPInstruction::computeCost and LoopVectorizationCostModel::getInstructionCost, with AArch64/SVE tests updated to reflect changed vectorization profitability and splice-cost diagnostics.
Changed symbols: VPInstruction::computeCost; LoopVectorizationCostModel::getInstructionCost
Behavioral change: Changes first-order recurrence splice costing from a concrete SmallVector mask with a VF-derived splice index to an empty mask and splice index -1.; Can alter profitability decisions and therefore whether or how LoopVectorize selects vectorization for first-order recurrence loops.; Does not, in the retrieved candidate hunks, alter VPlan recipe insertion, phi classification, recipe ordering, or plan CFG construction.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; SmallVector; VPInstruction::computeCost; No phi-like recipe ordering diagnostic appears in the candidate hunks.
Reproducer link: The added splice-cost test checks debug cost output for a first-order recurrence under AArch64 SVE.; No retrieved test or hunk references crash-62b480.cpp or an assertion failure.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize cost model; VPlan recipe cost computation; TargetTransformInfo splice costing
Causal explanation: The commit is in the relevant vectorizer/VPlan area and removes a local SmallVector used to form a cost-model mask, so it could indirectly change which vectorization plan is chosen. But the visible changes are limited to cost queries and expected profitability/output; they do not manipulate the SmallVector-backed VPlan recipe storage implicated by the issue or establish a phi-like recipe ordering change. The first-parent-distance-4 VPlanTransforms hunks are context only and are not candidate changes.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Changes production cost-model calls in both VPlanRecipes.cpp and LoopVectorize.cpp.; Adds an asserts-only debug-output test for splice cost, which provides targeted testability for the intended cost change.; Retrieved coverage is incomplete: 203 hunks were omitted.

top_candidates.subject: [LV] Add support for absolute difference partial reductions (#188043)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This LoopVectorize/VPlan feature commit adds support for recognizing and optimizing absolute-difference partial reductions. It introduces VPlan pattern matching for widened intrinsics, matches `abs(sub(ext(A), ext(B)))` reduction operands, and inserts new freeze, min/max, subtraction, and extension recipes into VPlans to compute the absolute difference at the narrower source type before partial reduction.
Changed symbols: m_WidenIntrinsic; optimizeExtendsForPartialReduction; matchExtendedReductionOperand; VPBuilder::insert; VPWidenIntrinsicRecipe; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/partial-reduce-usabs.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/partial-reduce-usabs.ll
Behavioral change: Recognizes widened `llvm.abs` of a subtraction of matching zero- or sign-extended operands as an absolute-difference reduction pattern.; Rewrites the matched pattern by inserting `freeze` recipes, signed or unsigned `max` and `min` widened-intrinsic recipes, a widened subtraction recipe, and a final zero-extension for the partial reduction.; Extends `VPBuilder::insert` to return the inserted typed recipe, enabling chained construction of newly inserted VPlan recipes.; Adds VPlan and generated-IR tests that expect a `WIDEN-REDUCTION-PHI` followed by the new non-phi widened recipes in a vector loop.
Assertion or trace link: The commit directly inserts multiple non-phi `VPRecipe` instances into VPlan blocks.; Its new VPlan test explicitly contains a `WIDEN-REDUCTION-PHI` and subsequently inserted non-phi recipes.; No retrieved hunk explicitly references or changes the assertion "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe".
Reproducer link: The added reproducer tests are AArch64 absolute-difference partial reductions, not the reported `crash-62b480.cpp` O3 input.; The transformed VPlan shape combines a reduction phi with newly created recipes, which is structurally relevant to the reported phi-like/non-phi ordering failure.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms; LoopVectorizationPlanner
Causal explanation: This is a plausible bisect candidate because it changes VPlan construction and insertion ordering in a reduction path: `VPBuilder(BinOp)` inserts several non-phi recipes relative to an existing recipe, while the tested plan also contains a reduction phi. The retrieved evidence does not prove that these insertions can place a phi-like recipe after a non-phi recipe, nor does it connect the new absolute-difference pattern to the reported source reproducer, so the link is moderate rather than definitive.
Causal confidence: 0.46
Build risk: Production VPlan transformation and planner API change.; Template change to `VPBuilder::insert` can affect callers expecting insertion-only behavior, although the visible change preserves insertion and merely returns the inserted pointer.; New AArch64-specific VPlan and IR tests cover the intended partial-reduction transformation.; The transformation relies on asserted matching assumptions for equal extension opcodes after pattern matching.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlan reverse-access reapplication changes reverse memory-access representation from a `VPWidenLoadRecipe`/`VPWidenStoreRecipe` reverse flag to explicit reverse operations, allowing reverse loads and stores to participate in mask-to-EVL optimization. new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e047d6ce009e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/clang/test/Driver/linux-ld-args.c
@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+/// Tests that gnutools::Linker::ConstructJob forwards user command-line options
+/// to the ld invocation. Sysroot-dependent toolchain discovery and
+/// crt*/library-path selection live in linux-ld.c.
+
+/// Mixed -Xlinker, -Wl, and standalone forwarding. -T is reordered to the end
+/// so that earlier -L paths take precedence.
+// RUN: %clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu -### \
+// RUN:   -e _start -T a.lds -t -Xlinker one -Xlinker --no-demangle \
+// RUN:   -Wl,two,--no-demangle,three -Xlinker four -z five -r %s 2>&1 | \
+// RUN:   FileCheck --check-prefix=MIXED %s
+// MIXED: "--no-demangle" "-e" "_start" "one" "two" "three" "four" "-z" "five" "-r" {{.*}} "-T" "a.lds" "-t"
+
+/// Passthrough flags. -rdynamic becomes -export-dynamic; -Wl,-z keyword pairs
+/// are forwarded as separate "-z" KEYWORD tokens.
+// RUN: %clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu -### \
+// RUN:   -s -u my_sym -rdynamic -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now %s 2>&1 | \
+// RUN:   FileCheck --check-prefix=PASS %s
+// PASS:      "-s"
+// PASS-SAME: "-export-dynamic"
+// PASS-SAME: "-u" "my_sym"
+// PASS-SAME: "-z" "relro" "-z" "now"
+
+/// -nopie is OpenBSD-specific.
+// RUN: not %clang -### --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu %s -nopie 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CHECK-NOPIE
+// CHECK-NOPIE: error: unsupported option '-nopie' for target 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'
